## Problem

The private-address guard from audit-e4e0a1a7 runs only in followRedirects and validExpandedURL, and those walk the HEAD chain through redirectClient. getPageTitle then GETs the final URL through httpClient, which has no CheckRedirect and so follows up to ten redirects with no host check (main.go:127-130). A bookmarked host can answer HEAD with 200 and GET with a 302 to http://192.168.1.1/ or http://169.254.169.254/. The tool then fetches that page and writes its <title> into the bookmark on Pinboard, which is exactly what the guard's docstring at main.go:1221-1225 says it prevents. confirmWithGet (main.go:1409) and fixParenthesesSuffix (main.go:1432) use the same unguarded client.

## Evidence

main.go:127-130: `var httpClient = &http.Client{ Timeout: defaultHTTPTimeout, Transport: newUserAgentTransport(), }` sets no CheckRedirect. main.go:1060: `resp, err := httpClient.Get(urlString)`. Reproduced in a scratch copy: isPublicHost was swapped to reject a second httptest server, and a first server answered HEAD 200 and GET 302 to the second. processBookmark returned `action=1 newTitle="INTERNAL ROUTER ADMIN" guardCalls=[]`, so the guard was never consulted.

## Impact

The title of an internal page reachable from the machine running the tool (router admin, cloud metadata, intranet) is written to a third-party service. For a shared bookmark that title is public. Severity matches audit-e4e0a1a7: the attacker must control a bookmarked host.

## Fix

Give httpClient a CheckRedirect that applies the same guard: `CheckRedirect: func(req *http.Request, via []*http.Request) error { if len(via) >= maxRedirectHops { return http.ErrUseLastResponse }; if !isPublicHost(req.URL.String()) { return fmt.Errorf("%w: redirect to non-public host %q", errUnverifiable, req.URL.Host) }; return nil }`. Note maxRedirectHops is declared after httpClient, so move the const up. Add a test mirroring the reproduction that asserts getPageTitle returns an error and RecordTitleFetch counts a failure.

## Resolution
checker.client has CheckRedirect = checkRedirect, which stops at maxRedirectHops (moved to the const block) and refuses non-public targets with errUnverifiable; it covers getPageTitle, confirmWithGet, fixParenthesesSuffix and the Pinboard calls. Tests: TestGetPageTitle_RefusesRedirectToNonPublicHost (reproduction: GET 302 into a host the guard rejects → error, no title), TestGetPageTitle_StopsAtHopLimit.
title: The title fetch follows GET redirects through httpClient with no isPublicHost check, so a host can steer it to a private address whose title is posted to Pinboard

## Problem

knownURLs is filled once from posts/all and never updated (main.go:265-271: "Filled once in run(), read-only afterwards"). When two bookmarks resolve to the same destination and the account did not already hold it (bit.ly/a and tinyurl.com/b both pointing at one article), applyUpdateWrite finds the target unknown for both. It issues two posts/add calls with replace=yes, so the second silently overwrites the first. This is the merge rule mergeIntoExisting exists to enforce ("The destination is the entry the user curated; the mover is the duplicate"), skipped only because the destination was created during this same run.

## Evidence

main.go:860 `if urlToUpdate != action.Original.URL && knownURLs[urlToUpdate] {` is the only merge check, and nothing on the success path at main.go:875-884 adds urlToUpdate to knownURLs. Reproduced in a scratch copy: two ActionUpdate actions with NewURL `https://example.org/article`, through applyBookmarkActions against a recording server, produced `url=https://example.org/article extended=notes-A tags=tagA replace=yes` then `url=https://example.org/article extended=notes-B tags=tagB replace=yes`, with stats `merged=0 updates=2`.

## Impact

The account ends with one bookmark carrying B's notes, tags, and creation date, and A's are discarded. The report says "Updates performed: 2" and "Duplicates merged: 0", which hides that two bookmarks collapsed into one. The Merged counter's own comment (statistics.go:78-82) calls that hiding a defect. The data loss is the same one bookmark the merge rule would drop, so the defect is the overwrite path and the misreport, plus one wasted rate-limited write.

## Fix

In applyUpdateWrite, after `stats.IncrementUpdates()` and before the `urlToUpdate == action.Original.URL` early return, add `knownURLs[urlToUpdate] = true`. The apply phase is sequential, so this still needs no mutex. Reword the knownURLs comment to say the apply phase extends it as it writes. Add a test with two actions sharing one unknown NewURL that asserts exactly one posts/add, two posts/delete, Merged == 1 and UpdatesPerformed == 1.

## Resolution
applyUpdateWrite records knownURLs[target] = true after a successful write to a changed URL, so a later mover to the same address merges instead of overwriting. Dry run records it too, so the preview matches. knownURLs docstring updated. Tests: TestApplyBookmarkActions_ConvergingMoversMerge (one posts/add carrying the first mover's fields, Merged 1, UpdatesPerformed 1), TestApplyBookmarkActions_DryRunPreviewsConvergingMoverAsMerge, TestApplyUpdateWrite_NewTargetIsWritten.
title: Two bookmarks moving to the same new URL are both written with replace=yes; the second overwrites the first and the report shows two updates and zero merges

## Problem

applyUpdateAction calls applyUpdateWrite, which returns nothing, and then prints the success narration whenever -verbose is set. It cannot know whether the write succeeded, failed, or was routed to mergeIntoExisting, which deletes the bookmark rather than updating it. Under -dry-run it skips the write and prints the same "Updated:" lines, while the delete path prints "Would delete:" (main.go:936). The dry-run preview of a merge therefore claims an update for a bookmark the real run would delete.

## Evidence

main.go:914-916: `if !dryRun { applyUpdateWrite(action, apiToken) }`, followed unconditionally at main.go:922-930 by `fmt.Printf("Updated: %s -> %s\n", ...)`, `"Added title: %s\n"` and `"Added tags: %s\n"`. applyUpdateWrite's failure path (main.go:868-872) and its merge path (main.go:860-863) both just return. A real merge under -verbose prints both "Merged: X already bookmarked as Y; removed the duplicate" (main.go:908) and "Updated: X -> Y". No test asserts any of these lines (rg for "Updated: " finds only main.go:923).

## Impact

README.md:194 recommends `-dry-run -verbose` to preview a run. For every bookmark that would be merged, the preview says "Updated" when the real run deletes it and its notes. In real runs, the verbose log shows a failed write as both an error and a success.

## Fix

Have applyUpdateWrite return its outcome (`type writeOutcome int` with outcomeUpdated, outcomeMerged, outcomeFailed). In dry run, derive the would-be outcome with the same `urlToUpdate != action.Original.URL && knownURLs[urlToUpdate]` test, without writing. Print "Updated:" / "Added …" only for outcomeUpdated, prefix them "Would " under dry run, and print "Would merge: X into Y" for a dry-run merge. Add report tests for the failed, merged and dry-run cases that assert the absence of "Updated:".

## Resolution
applyUpdateWrite returns a writeOutcome (updated/merged/failed); applyUpdateAction derives the would-be outcome in dry run, and narrateUpdate prints by outcome: nothing for failed, 'Merged:' or 'Would merge:' for merges, 'Updated:'/'Added …' with a 'Would ' form under -dry-run. Test: TestApplyUpdateAction_NarratesTheOutcome (update, rejected write, merge, dry-run update, dry-run merge).
title: -verbose prints "Updated:" / "Added title:" / "Added tags:" for writes that failed, for merges that deleted the bookmark instead, and for dry runs

## Problem

processBookmarksParallel takes a semaphore slot (main.go:799) before the goroutine starts. The goroutine then calls waitForHost, which reserves the next slot for that host and sleeps until it comes (main.go:205-214). When consecutive bookmarks in posts/all share a host, every worker reserves a successively later slot on that host and sleeps. Bookmarks for other hosts cannot start until a worker frees up, so the pool runs at 1/perHostInterval requests per second, not at -workers width. This happens on any day-of-import or one-site reading session, since posts/all is ordered by date.

## Evidence

main.go:799 `sem <- struct{}{}` happens before the goroutine, and main.go:214 `time.Sleep(time.Until(slot))` runs inside it. Reproduced in a scratch copy with perHostInterval = 100ms and 10 workers: 20 bookmarks on host A followed by one on host B. Host B's first request arrived after 1.001s, exactly ten reserved A-slots, though B had no throttle of its own. README.md:317-318 claims the opposite: "Different hosts are never throttled against each other, so the pool still runs at full width."

## Impact

At the 500ms default, 100 clustered bookmarks on one domain hold all workers for about 50 seconds per request round. Every other host's bookmarks queue behind them, so a run takes roughly the sum of per-host times instead of the maximum.

## Fix

Interleave hosts before dispatch, so consecutive work items rarely share a host. In processBookmarksParallel, bucket bookmarks by `url.Parse(b.URL).Host` in first-seen order, then emit them round-robin across buckets. Collected results stay order-independent, since phase 2 already applies them in arrival order. Add a test mirroring the reproduction: 20 A-bookmarks then one B-bookmark, 10 workers and a 100ms interval, asserting B is requested within the first interval. Alternatively, change README.md:317-318 to state the limitation.

## Resolution
processBookmarksParallel dispatches interleaveHosts(bookmarks): round-robin across hosts, each host's own order kept. README 'Bookmarked hosts' now describes the dealing. Tests: TestInterleaveHosts (order, unparseable URL bucket), TestProcessBookmarksParallel_OneHostDoesNotParkThePool (20 A-bookmarks then one B, 100ms interval: B requested within the first interval).
title: waitForHost sleeps while holding a worker slot, so a run of same-host bookmarks parks the whole pool and other hosts wait behind it

## Problem

cli ignores godotenv.Load's return value on the assumption that the only error is a missing file. godotenv parses the whole file before setting anything, and any parse error aborts the load. A .env with a valid PINBOARD_API_TOKEN line and one malformed line elsewhere therefore loads nothing. The user then sees "Error: API token is required (set PINBOARD_API_TOKEN or pass -token)", which points at the one thing they did set.

## Evidence

main.go:322-323: `// A .env file is optional; a missing one is not an error.` / `_ = godotenv.Load() //nolint:errcheck // .env file is optional`. Reproduced in a scratch copy: a .env of `PINBOARD_API_TOKEN=user:abc` followed by `this is not valid` gives `Load err=unexpected character "\n" in variable name near "this is not valid\n" token=""`.

## Impact

The real cause, a parse error at a named line, is hidden behind a wrong diagnosis. A permission error on .env is hidden the same way. A scheduled run fails every time until someone reads the .env by hand.

## Fix

Ignore only the missing-file case: `if err := godotenv.Load(); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) { fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "Error reading .env: %v\n", err); return 1 }`, which needs the io/fs import. Drop the `//nolint:errcheck`. Add a cli test that writes a malformed .env under t.TempDir() and t.Chdir, asserting exit code 1 and the "Error reading .env" message.

## Resolution
configure ignores only fs.ErrNotExist from godotenv.Load; any other error prints 'Error reading .env: …' to stderr and exits 1. The errcheck nolint is gone. Test: TestCLI_MalformedDotEnvExitsOne (t.TempDir + t.Chdir, malformed line → exit 1 and the message).
title: godotenv.Load's error is discarded whatever it is, so one malformed .env line drops the token silently and the run fails with "API token is required"

## Problem

Both tests call the function under test and stop. TestCloseBody_ReportsFailure's docstring says it proves "closeBody's failure branch routes to stderr rather than stdout", but it captures neither stream. Its inline comment "Closing twice makes the second Close return an error deterministically" describes code that is not there; errCloser simply always fails. run_test.go TestCloseBody_ReportsFailure body: `t.Parallel()` / `closeBody(errCloser{})`, with no t.Error or t.Fatal. TestReportApplyError_HonoursVerbose body: `setVerbose(t, true)` / `reportApplyError("updating", testURL, errors.New("boom"))` / `setVerbose(t, false)` / `reportApplyError(...)`, with no assertion. For reportApplyError: capture stderr under each verbose setting, and assert "Error updating" appears when true and the output is empty when false. Delete the "Closing twice" comment.

## Resolution
TestCloseBody_ReportsFailure asserts 'close failed' on the diagnostic stream and nothing on the report stream; the wrong 'Closing twice' comment is gone. TestReportApplyError_HonoursVerbose asserts the line is printed under -verbose and absent without it. Both run in parallel on their own checker.
title: TestCloseBody_ReportsFailure and TestReportApplyError_HonoursVerbose assert nothing; they execute the branches for the 100% gate and pass whatever is printed

## Problem

The archive config publishes every non-Windows build twice: as a tar.gz carrying LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and README.md, and as a bare `binary` upload. GoReleaser uploads a `binary`-format artifact directly with no `files`, and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md is not attached to the release by any other route. Nothing configures release.extra_files. A user who downloads the bare binary therefore receives golang.org/x/net, x/sys and x/term, all BSD-3-Clause, without the notice their clause 2 requires. gen-notices.sh:4-7 states that requirement itself.

## Evidence

.goreleaser.yml:65: `formats: ["binary", "tar.gz"]`. Windows is overridden to zip-only at :66-68, so the bare binaries are the linux, darwin and freebsd builds. .goreleaser.yml:73-79 lists the files that go into archives only. GoReleaser archive docs (goreleaser.com/customization/archive): "If format is `binary`, no archives are created and the binaries are instead uploaded directly." The x/net, x/sys and x/term LICENSE files begin "Redistribution and use in source and binary forms…", the BSD-3 text. `GOOS={linux,darwin,windows,freebsd} go list -deps` yields the same seven modules, so the notice content itself is complete.

## Impact

Those release assets are a binary redistribution that does not meet the BSD-3 attribution condition. That is the exact defect gen-notices.sh and the archive comment at .goreleaser.yml:75-77 exist to prevent, so the README's statement that releases ship the notices does not hold for these files.

## Fix

Either drop the bare format (`formats: ["tar.gz"]`), which is the simplest option, since the archives already carry everything. Or attach the notices to every release with `release: extra_files: [{glob: ./THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md}, {glob: ./LICENSE}]`. That way each downloadable binary sits beside its notices on the release page.

## Resolution
.goreleaser.yml archives formats is now ["tar.gz"] (windows stays zip), with a comment explaining why the bare 'binary' format is excluded. Every downloadable binary now ships inside an archive carrying LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. goreleaser check validates the config.
title: The raw "binary" release assets ship the BSD-3 dependencies with no notices: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md exists only inside the tar.gz/zip archives and the packages

## Problem

Three user-facing statements contradict the code. (1) The -ci flag help and README.md:150 say CI mode means "no progress bar or verbose output". ciMode gates only the two progress bars and the summary, so `-ci -verbose` prints every verbose line, and the help text never mentions that -ci suppresses the summary. (2) README.md:223 introduces "Two counters are worth knowing:" and then lists three: Skipped, Writes rejected, Duplicates merged. (3) .goreleaser.yml:115-116, the header of every GitHub release, describes the tool as one that "reports dead links". It deletes them (main.go:3: "removes links the server reports as gone").

## Evidence

main.go:330: `flagSet.BoolVar(&ciMode, "ci", false, "CI mode (no progress bar or verbose output)")`. ciMode is read only at main.go:460 (summary), main.go:783 and main.go:968 (progress bars), and no verbose print checks it, e.g. main.go:662 `if verbose { fmt.Printf("Processing: %s\n", b.URL) }`. README.md:223: "counters are worth knowing:" followed by bullets at README.md:225, :228 and :230. .goreleaser.yml:115-116: "Checks and repairs Pinboard bookmarks: expands shortened URLs, follows redirects, fills in missing titles and tags, and reports dead links."

## Impact

A user who reads the release notes before a first run is told the tool only reports dead links, and it permanently deletes them. A CI job that combines -ci with -verbose for diagnostics gets every bookmark URL, private ones included, in its log, contrary to the help text. The miscount is cosmetic.

## Fix

(1) Change the help string to "CI mode: no progress bars and no summary; failures still reach stderr", and README.md:150 to match. Either keep -verbose independent, or make -ci win by gating the verbose prints on `verbose && !ciMode`, and state which. (2) README.md:223: "Three counters are worth knowing:". (3) .goreleaser.yml:116: "fills in missing titles and tags, and deletes bookmarks whose server reports them gone (404/410)".

## Resolution
-ci help: 'CI mode: no progress bars; the summary becomes one count line on stderr'. README:150 matches and states that -verbose still narrates alongside -ci. README Statistics says 'Three counters'. The .goreleaser.yml release header says the tool deletes bookmarks whose server reports them gone (404/410).
title: -ci help text promises "no verbose output" though -ci -verbose prints all of it; README says "Two counters" then lists three; the release header says the tool "reports" dead links it deletes

## Problem

expandURL, shortenerFor, shortenerServices, unshortenBitlyImpl, unshortenTinyURLImpl, unshortenIsGdImpl, validExpandedURL, the bitlyEndpoint and isGdEndpoint seams, the BITLY_ACCESS_TOKEN variable, and the ShortURLsExpanded/ShortURLsFailed report all exist to resolve a short link to its destination. followRedirects already does that for any host. ## Evidence

main.go:1589-1601: unshortenTinyURLImpl is `redirectClient.Head(shortURL)` then `resp.Location()`, which is the same pair of calls checkURL makes at main.go:1345 and main.go:1371. main.go:1475-1481 returns the short URL unchanged when expansion fails, and main.go:1276 then sends it to followRedirects. Observed 2026-10-26: `curl -sI https://bit.ly/github` → `HTTP/2 301` + `location:`; `curl -sI https://is.gd/github` → `HTTP/2 301` + `location: http://github.com/...`.

## Impact

About 200 lines of production code plus their tests, two package-level endpoint seams, an extra credential, and a report section all maintain a second resolution path whose result followRedirects already produces. Each shortener added means a new expander, a new stats key and new docs. The duplication already let the docs drift: README says bit.ly links are untouched without a token, but the redirect walk expands them.

## Fix

Delete the expandURL repair step and everything only it uses (shortenerFor, shortenerService, shortenerServices, the three unshorten*Impl functions and their variables, validExpandedURL, bitlyEndpoint, isGdEndpoint, bitlyTokenName, errNoBitlyToken, svc* constants, RecordShortenerExpansion, printShortenerStats, ShortURLsExpanded/Failed). repairSteps then holds only fixParenthesesSuffix. Delete their tests and the BITLY_ACCESS_TOKEN lines in README.md and .env.example. The one thing the Bitly API adds is bypassing Bitly's interstitial warning page for flagged links. If that is wanted, keep only unshortenBitlyImpl, behind the token, and record the reason next to it.

## Resolution
Deleted expandURL, shortenerFor, shortenerService(s), the three unshorten*Impl and their seams, validExpandedURL, the bit.ly and is.gd endpoints, bitlyTokenName, errNoBitlyToken, svc* constants, RecordShortenerExpansion, printShortenerStats and the ShortURLs* counters. With one step left, the urlStep/repairSteps pipeline went too: expandAndCheckURL is followRedirects(fixParenthesesSuffix(u)). The only coverage:ignore marker left with unshortenBitlyImpl (README Coverage section updated: none today). Production statements went from 710 to 618 before the refactor. Short links resolve through the redirect walk, verified live on 2026-10-26: bit.ly and is.gd answer HEAD with 301.
title: The three shortener API expanders duplicate followRedirects: bit.ly, is.gd and tinyurl all answer HEAD with a 301 that the redirect walk already follows

## Problem

Three kinds of configuration do nothing, or less than they appear to. (1) `gosec.includes` restricts gosec to ten rules, so `gosec.excludes: [G204, G304]` excludes rules that never run. The allowlist also silently disables the other ~40 gosec rules (G107, G110, G112, G114, G115, G3xx file permissions, G5xx crypto imports, …) while the block reads as a full gosec setup. (2) Several settings name identifiers no file in this repo contains: `misspell.ignore-rules: [tmux]`, wrapcheck `ignore-sigs` for `errutil.New(`, `errutil.LogAndWrap(` and `.WithStack(`, revive var-naming's `["VM"]` deny list, and varnamelen `ignore-names` `tm`, `ui` and `id`. They read as copied template defaults, but each one still looks like a decision someone made.

## Evidence

.golangci.yml:129-142: `excludes: - G204 - G304` alongside `includes:` listing G101, G102, G103, G104, G201, G202, G401, G402, G403, G404, with neither G204 nor G304 among them. .golangci.yml:146-147 `tmux`, :224-227 `errutil.*`, :204 `["VM"]`, :168-174 `tm`/`ui`/`id`. `rg` over *.go finds 0 occurrences of tmux, errutil, Wrapf, WithMessage, WithStack, \bVM\b, \btm\b, \bui\b or \bid\b. Standalone gosec with every rule enabled (this run) reports only the two G101 env-var names already `//nolint:gosec`'d, so dropping the allowlist costs nothing today.

## Impact

A reader cannot tell which settings protect this code and which are inert. gosec checks a quarter of its rules, so a future G110, G115 or G304-class defect would pass lint even though the config appears to enable gosec.

## Fix

Lint configuration changes only with the owner's explicit approval. Delete `gosec.includes` and the then-pointless `gosec.excludes`, so gosec runs every rule (verified clean today apart from the two annotated G101 lines). Delete the `tmux` misspell rule, the `errutil.*`, `.Wrap(`, `.Wrapf(`, `.WithMessage(`, `.WithMessagef(` and `.WithStack(` wrapcheck signatures, the revive `["VM"]` deny list, and the `tm`, `ui` and `id` varnamelen names. Re-run `golangci-lint run --fix=false` and confirm 0 issues.

## Resolution
Applied with the owner's explicit approval. Removed gosec includes/excludes (gosec now runs every rule), misspell ignore-rules tmux, the revive VM deny list (now []), the varnamelen tm/ui/id names, and the wrapcheck .Wrap/.Wrapf/.WithMessage/.WithMessagef/.WithStack/errutil.* signatures (.Errorf(, errors.New( and errors.Unwrap( kept). golangci-lint config verify passes; golangci-lint run reports 0 issues.
title: .golangci.yml carries dead and narrowing entries: gosec excludes that cannot apply, a 10-rule gosec allowlist, and template settings for names this repo never uses

## Problem

Class: non-gating-check (absent gate). Source: manual. go.yml runs the build, the race and coverage gate, and golangci-lint, and nothing else. The repo declares `max_line_length = 100` and other rules in .editorconfig, ships two bash scripts on the release path (gen-notices.sh runs as a goreleaser hook), and maintains two workflows. No tool for any of these is pinned in mise.toml ([tools] holds golangci-lint, goreleaser, cosign and syft only), and no CI step checks them. A contributor can only check them with tools from their own global setup, at whatever version that happens to be.

## Evidence

mise.toml:9-15 lists four tools. go.yml defines two jobs, `build` (mise run build, mise run coverage) and `lint` (golangci-lint-action), and neither runs editorconfig-checker, shellcheck, actionlint or zizmor. The resolved ledger holds five defects of exactly these kinds, each found by an audit rather than CI: audit-4d07eb24 ("EditorConfig violations: three workflow lines exceed max_line_length 100"), audit-491d4b7d (findings-store files violating max_line_length), audit-d0bae068 ("shellcheck SC2129 in gen-notices.sh"), ci-4d539695 (zizmor artipacked) and ci-2f8ac725 (zizmor anonymous-definition). All four tools pass on today's tree, verified with known-positive controls this run, so a gate can be added without first fixing anything.

## Impact

The next violation of each kind lands silently, as the last five did. For gen-notices.sh, a shell defect surfaces only at tag time, inside the job holding contents: write and the signing identity.

## Fix

Pin the four tools in mise.toml [tools] (`editorconfig-checker`, `shellcheck`, `actionlint`, `zizmor`, at the versions the release uses). Add one task: `[tasks.check] run = ["editorconfig-checker", "shellcheck scripts/*.sh", "actionlint", "zizmor --pedantic ."]`. Run `mise run check` as a step in go.yml's `lint` job after mise-action. Name the job in the ci-c9be5b98 ruleset so it gates.

## Resolution
mise.toml pins editorconfig-checker 4.0.2, shellcheck 0.11.0, actionlint 1.7.12 and zizmor 1.31.1, and adds [tasks.check] running all four. go.yml's Lint job runs 'mise run check' after mise-action. README Testing/Contributing name the task. The gate caught a line-length violation in this very change before it landed. It becomes a required check once ci-c9be5b98's ruleset names the Lint job.
title: CI checks only Go: .editorconfig, the shell scripts and the workflows have no pinned checker and no CI step, and five defects of those kinds have already reached the tree

## Problem

The fix for audit-cab2c599 stops temporary redirects (302/303/307) from rewriting the bookmark URL. The title fetch still follows them. fetchTitleIfNeeded calls getPageTitle on the kept URL, and getPageTitle GETs it through c.client, which follows redirects. For an untitled bookmark behind a login wall, the GET lands on the login page, and that page's <title> is written to the bookmark as its title. The URL logic and the title logic now disagree about the same redirect.

## Evidence

main.go:1428 `resp, err := c.client.Get(urlString)`. c.client's CheckRedirect (checkRedirect) only bounds hops and refuses non-public hosts, so it follows a 302. Reproduced in a scratch copy: a server 302s every path to /login, and /login serves `<title>Sign in to Example</title>`. `processBookmark(Bookmark{URL: srv/private/doc, Tags: "x"})` returned `action=1 NewURL=".../private/doc" NewTitle="Sign in to Example"`: an ActionUpdate that posts the login page's title.

## Impact

Every untitled bookmark of a session-gated page gets the login page's title, typically one generic string across a whole site. Nothing is lost, since the title was empty, but a wrong title is written to the user's account, and the report counts it as "Titles added".

## Fix

In getPageTitle, take no title from a page the GET was redirected to. followRedirects has already moved the URL through every permanent hop, so a further redirect here is temporary or GET-only. After the status check, add `if resp.Request.URL.String() != urlString { return "", nil }`, which RecordTitleFetch counts as nothing to add. Add a test mirroring the reproduction, asserting NewTitle == "" and ActionNoChange. Extend README "How It Works" ("Fetches page title if bookmark has no title") with "— not from a page it was temporarily redirected to".

## Resolution
getPageTitle uses c.redirectClient, so it no longer follows redirects. A redirect answer is a non-200 like any other and no title is taken; the target is never requested. This follows a different route from the proposed `resp.Request.URL` comparison: it makes no request to the login page and adds no branch. The docstrings of getPageTitle, the client fields and checkRedirect are updated; checkRedirect now guards only the GET re-check and the parenthesis probe. README 'How It Works' names the behavior. Tests: TestGetPageTitle_TakesNoTitleThroughARedirect covers 301/302/303/307/308. The two getPageTitle redirect tests that were the only coverage of checkRedirect moved to TestConfirmWithGet_RefusesRedirectToNonPublicHost and _StopsAtHopLimit. Mutation of each guard was killed.
title: An untitled bookmark behind a temporary redirect gets the redirect target's title: a login-walled page is retitled "Sign in…" while its URL is correctly kept

## Problem

rateLimiter is a time.Ticker, and wait() receives from ticker.C, so the first call of a run blocks until the first tick, a whole interval after construction. Pinboard's budget is one call per interval between calls; nothing requires the first call to wait. Separately, rateLimiter.current() has no production caller: it was added for the tests, which could read the field directly.

## Evidence

main.go:166 `ticker: time.NewTicker(interval)` and main.go:173 `<-r.ticker.C`. Reproduced in a scratch copy: `newChecker(...).getBookmarks()` against a local server took `3s`. TestCLI_FetchFailureExitsNonZero, the only test running a production-configured checker, accounts for 3 of the suite's ~6 s. `rg '\.current\(\)'` finds 0 references in main.go/statistics.go and 5 in *_test.go.

## Impact

Every run idles 3 s before fetching posts/all, and the test suite pays the same 3 s. The ticker also needs Reset bookkeeping in widen and narrow that a next-slot timestamp would not.

## Fix

Replace the ticker with a next-slot time: `type rateLimiter struct { mu sync.Mutex; base, interval time.Duration; next time.Time }`. wait() locks, runs `time.Sleep(time.Until(r.next))`, then sets `r.next = time.Now().Add(r.interval)`. widen() doubles the interval (clamped) and sets `r.next = time.Now().Add(r.interval)`, so the retry after a 429 waits the widened interval. narrow() only halves toward base. The first call then goes immediately, and the hold-the-lock-across-the-wait property that makes the budget global is unchanged. Delete current() and have the tests read `limiter.interval`. Add a test that a fresh limiter's first wait() returns in well under its interval and the second waits at least one.

## Resolution
rateLimiter replaces the time.Ticker with a `next` slot. wait sleeps until next, then books next = now + interval, so the zero value lets the first call go at once. widen sets next = now + the new interval. narrow only halves toward base; its interval<=base guard is gone because max() already floors it. current() is deleted, and the tests read limiter.interval directly. Tests: TestRateLimiter_FirstCallDoesNotWait (1h interval returns at once) and TestRateLimiter_SpacesCallsByTheInterval (spacing plus widened spacing). Three mutations were each killed.
title: rateLimiter waits a full interval before the first Pinboard call (3 s per run, 3 s per CLI test); its current() accessor exists only for tests

## Problem

The apply-phase bar draws on stdout as "\r<frame>" and leaves the cursor at the end of the frame. recordDeletion writes "deleted (…): …\n" to stderr. On a terminal, where both streams share one screen, the record starts mid-line right after the frame, so each record reads as a continuation of a progress-bar line. That is the default mode (no -ci), and the records exist to be read and replayed after a wrongful deletion.

## Evidence

main.go:1415 `fmt.Fprintf(c.errOut, "deleted (%s): %s\n", ...)`. main.go:1027-1043 (progressBar.increment) writes `"\r%-*s"` with no newline until the last item. Reproduced in a scratch copy with stdout and stderr on one buffer and two dead-link deletions: `"\rApplying changes...  50% |████████████████████                    | (1/2) [0s:0s]deleted (dead link): …"`.

## Impact

A user copying a record to restore a bookmark has to cut a bar frame off its front first. The README's "Deletion records" example shows the line starting with `deleted (`, which is not what the terminal shows.

## Fix

Let the active bar give up its line before a record is written. Give progressBar a `breakLine()` method that, under its lock, writes "\n" when a frame is on screen (done > 0 && done < total) and resets longest. Keep the apply bar on the checker during applyBookmarkActions (`c.applyBar = bar`, cleared after the loop), and call `c.applyBar.breakLine()` at the top of recordDeletion; a nil bar makes it a no-op under -ci. Add a test with out and errOut on one buffer asserting every "deleted (" occurrence starts a line.

## Resolution
progressBar.breakLine writes a newline when a frame is on screen (0 < done < total); nil-safe. applyBookmarkActions keeps its bar on checker.applyBar (field documented; not cleared afterwards, since breakLine on a finished bar is a no-op). recordDeletion calls c.applyBar.breakLine() before the record. Tests: TestProgressBar_BreakLineOnlyMidBar (0/2, 1/2, 2/2), TestProgressBar_NilIgnoresCalls, and TestApplyBookmarkActions_DeletionRecordStartsItsOwnLine (three deletions, shared stream, every record at column 0). Mutations were killed. The -verbose variant of the same gluing is filed separately.
title: In a default interactive run, each deletion record is printed onto the end of the apply bar's line instead of a line of its own

## Problem

This branch replaced the fixed name list (`for f in LICENSE LICENSE.txt LICENSE.md COPYING NOTICE`) with a loop over every file in each module directory. The loop upper-cases each name and matches it against LICENSE*, LICENCE* and COPYING/NOTICE variants. The comment justifies this with github.com/joho/godotenv (LICENCE) and github.com/kr/pretty (License). The branch later removed godotenv and progressbar, so the only module the script now visits is golang.org/x/net, which ships a file named LICENSE. Neither example module is linked. The matcher no longer serves any requirement, and its comment cites dependencies the reader cannot find in go.mod.

## Evidence

`git diff main -- scripts/gen-notices.sh` shows the matcher is new on this branch. go.mod requires only golang.org/x/net v0.61.0. The S12 lens of this run confirmed the script emits exactly x/net. scripts/gen-notices.sh:40 names the two removed or unlinked modules.

## Impact

This is machinery and a misleading comment with no current user. A reader maintaining the release path has to work out why LICENCE and mixed-case names matter, and the answer is no longer in the repository.

## Fix

Go back to the fixed list, keeping this branch's hard failure: `found=0; for f in LICENSE LICENSE.txt LICENSE.md COPYING NOTICE; do [ -f "$dir/$f" ] || continue; found=1; ...; done`, followed by the existing `found -eq 0` exit. Shorten the comment to say that a module with none of these names fails the run, and that the name is added when that happens. The trade-off is that a future dependency with an unlisted name fails at tag time, loudly, rather than being matched. Run shellcheck and a goreleaser snapshot (`mise run release`) to confirm THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md still holds x/net's LICENSE.

## Resolution
gen-notices.sh is back on the fixed name list (LICENSE LICENSE.txt LICENSE.md COPYING NOTICE) and keeps the hard failure when a module matches none. That failure is what audit-a2cad624's "silently" required. The comment drops the removed-module examples and says to add the name when a new dependency trips it. Ran the script: wrote THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md with one module (golang.org/x/net v0.61.0, LICENSE), then removed the generated file. shellcheck is clean via mise run check.
title: gen-notices.sh scans every file with a case-insensitive six-pattern matcher, added for two modules the binary no longer links

## Problem

goreleaser groups the changelog by commit type and excludes `^chore:`. Two mistyped commits before v0.1.0 therefore misstate the only release. ba94f8b (`feat(github-action)!: Update actions/checkout (v4 → v5)`), a822d34 and dd33ba8 (`feat(github-action): update go …`) change only workflow files, yet appear under "🚀 Features", and ba94f8b is flagged breaking. e8e8227 `chore: updates, fixes and refactoring` changes 8 files (+1268/−155), main.go included, and is filtered out entirely.

## Evidence

`git show --name-only ba94f8b a822d34 dd33ba8` touches only .github/workflows/go.yml and release.yml. `git show --shortstat e8e8227` gives 8 files changed, 1268 insertions(+), 155 deletions(-). `gh release view v0.1.0` shows those three under "### 🚀 Features" and no entry for e8e8227. .goreleaser.yml:140-143 excludes `"^chore:"`. Newer Renovate action bumps are typed `chore(actions)` (e.g. 7980cee), so the generator has been corrected upstream.

## Impact

A reader of the release page sees a breaking feature that is a CI checkout bump, and does not see the fixes in e8e8227. The record is wrong, but nothing new is mis-typed, so the defect is confined to that one note.

## Fix

The repository owner edits the published note. Delete the three feat(github-action) lines and add a short Fixes entry summarizing e8e8227: `gh release view v0.1.0 --json body --jq .body > notes.md`, edit notes.md, then `gh release edit v0.1.0 --notes-file notes.md`. No config change is needed, because Renovate already emits chore(actions).

## Resolution
Edited the published v0.1.0 notes with `gh release edit v0.1.0 --notes-file`, as the owner asked. The three feat(github-action) lines (ba94f8b, a822d34, dd33ba8) moved from Features to the end of Other changes with their subjects verbatim. That departs from the proposed delete so the release still lists every commit it contains. Added two e8e8227 entries summarizing the commit: a Features entry (title fetching, suggested tags, parallel processing with a progress bar and rate limiting, -ci, .env token), and a Bug Fixes entry (the HEAD redirect check followed redirects itself, so it never saw a 301/302). An italic note under Changelog states the correction. Read back: the live body equals the corrected file apart from the trailing newline; 0 feat(github-action) lines remain under Features; the release is still neither draft nor prerelease. The original body is kept in the session scratchpad for revert.
title: The published v0.1.0 changelog lists three CI-only Renovate bumps as Features (one marked breaking) and omits e8e8227's fixes, which were committed as chore

## Problem

newProgressBar draws a bar whenever -ci is off, including under -verbose. The bar writes "\r<frame>" to the report stream and leaves the cursor at the end of the frame. Every verbose line goes to the same stream or to stderr: "Processing: …", "Fetched title: …", "Redirected URL updated: …", "Deleted: …", "Skipping …". Each one therefore starts right after the frame drawn before it. The fix for audit-ca0b8ce5 breaks the line only before a deletion record, which is the one line printed in the default mode.

## Evidence

Probe in a scratch copy, run with -verbose, one worker, three bookmarks, stdout and stderr on one buffer. Two lines were glued: "\rProcessing bookmarks...  33% |█████████████ … | (1/3) [0s:0s]Processing: http://127.0.0.1:36591/2", and the same at 2/3. main.go:866 prints "Processing: %s\n" to c.out from the workers while the bar draws on c.out.

## Impact

Verbose output, the mode used to see what a run did, has a bar frame in front of nearly every line. The narration already reports progress one bookmark at a time, so the bar adds nothing there.

## Fix

Draw no bar under -verbose: `if c.ciMode || c.verbose || total <= 0 { return nil }` in newProgressBar, with its docstring saying why. Extend TestNewProgressBar_OffUnderCIAndForNothing with the -verbose case. Have the README's "Progress Tracking" line and the -verbose description say verbose output replaces the bar.

## Resolution
Under -verbose, newProgressBar sets the bar's `every` to progressReportInterval (15s), as the owner specified: no bar, but a progress line every 15 s or so. In that mode increment prints `<description> N/T (P%), <elapsed> elapsed, <estimate> left` as a line of its own, at most once per interval, measured from the start and then from the last report. It never draws a "\r" frame. The check runs when an item finishes, so a line can be up to one item late; a ticker was not used because it needs a goroutine stopped per phase. breakLine is a no-op in this mode. remaining() is shared by the frame and the line. -ci still turns everything off. README Progress Tracking and the -verbose option describe it, and docs_test asserts "every 15 seconds" against the constant. Tests: TestProgressBar_ReportsALineEachInterval, TestNewProgressBar_ReportsUnderVerbose, TestProcessBookmarksParallel_VerboseDrawsNoFrames, and a report-mode case in TestProgressBar_BreakLineOnlyMidBar. All 5 mutations were killed.
title: Under -verbose, every narration line is printed onto the end of a progress-bar frame

## Problem

Class: non-gating-check. go.yml runs on `pull_request` to main and executes the build, `go test -race`, the 100% coverage gate and golangci-lint. Comments in the file and the README call these mandatory ("failing on it is the point", "All of them must pass"). None of them is a required status check.

## Evidence

Verified with gh authenticated as the repo owner (re-verified 2026-10-23 after the mise migration): `gh api repos/ivuorinen/pinboard-checker/branches/main/protection` → `Branch not protected (HTTP 404)`; `gh api repos/ivuorinen/pinboard-checker/rulesets` → `[]`; `gh api repos/ivuorinen/pinboard-checker/rules/branches/main` → `[]`. go.yml:55-56 `# Tests under -race plus the 100% gate ... failing on it is the point.`; README.md:296-297 `CI runs the build, the test suite under -race with the 100% coverage gate, and golangci-lint. All of them must pass.`

## Impact

A PR with a failing race test, a coverage drop or a lint error can be merged, by hand or by any Renovate automerge rule in the shared config, with red checks. The "100% is a contract" claim in coverage-gate.sh depends on a gate that GitHub does not enforce.

## Fix

The repository owner runs this; it is never applied automatically. The jobs are now named `Build and test` and `Lint` (go.yml). Once the workflow has run with those names on a PR, require both with a ruleset on the default branch:

`echo '{"name":"main","target":"branch","enforcement":"active","conditions":{"ref_name":{"include":["~DEFAULT_BRANCH"],"exclude":[]}},"rules":[{"type":"required_status_checks","parameters":{"strict_required_status_checks_policy":false,"required_status_checks":[{"context":"Build and test"},{"context":"Lint"}]}}]}' | gh api -X POST repos/ivuorinen/pinboard-checker/rulesets --input -`

Verify with `gh api repos/ivuorinen/pinboard-checker/rules/branches/main --jq '.[].parameters.required_status_checks[].context'`, which must print both names.

## Resolution
The owner created ruleset 25926686 ("main", enforcement active, target ~DEFAULT_BRANCH, no bypass actors). It has three rules: deletion, non_fast_forward, and required_status_checks requiring "Build and test" and "Lint", both pinned to integration 15368 (GitHub Actions), strict policy off. Verified with `gh api repos/ivuorinen/pinboard-checker/rules/branches/main` (lists all three rules and both contexts) and `gh api .../rulesets/25926686`. The two contexts are the job names this branch gives go.yml. Until it merges, main's workflow reports them as build/lint, so PRs on the old workflow (open: #76) cannot merge until rebased.
title: Build, test, coverage gate and lint gate nothing: main has no branch protection and no rulesets (Verified)
